title: IPO
prompt:
You are given `n` projects where the i-th project has a pure profit `profits[i]` and requires a minimum capital `capital[i]` to start. Initially you have `w` capital. When you finish a project, you gain its profit, which adds to your total capital.

You may pick at most `k` distinct projects to work on, in any order, choosing at each step any project whose capital requirement is currently met. Return the maximum total capital you can end up with after finishing at most `k` projects.

examples.explanation: With w=0, only project 0 (capital 0) is affordable. After finishing it, capital becomes 1, unlocking projects 1 and 2 (both need capital 1). Pick project 2 for profit 3, ending with capital 0+1+3=4.
The only project requires 10 capital but we start with 0 and have no finished projects to unlock it, so no project is ever affordable and capital stays at 0.

hints: At each step you want the most profitable project among those you can currently afford — but the set of affordable projects changes as your capital grows.
Sort projects by capital requirement, and use a pointer to add newly affordable projects (as capital grows) into a max-heap keyed by profit.
At each of the k rounds: push all projects now affordable into the max-heap, pop the most profitable one, add its profit to your capital, and repeat.

solution.approach: Sort projects by their capital requirement so we can incrementally reveal which ones are affordable as our capital grows. Use a max-heap (negated profits) to always pick the most profitable currently-affordable project. For each of up to k rounds: advance a pointer through the capital-sorted list, pushing every project whose capital requirement is now met into the max-heap; then pop the heap's maximum profit project (if any) and add it to our capital. Greedily taking the best affordable option each round is optimal because unlocking capital only ever grows the affordable set, so there's never a reason to save a top choice for later.
solution.code:
import heapq

def ipo(k, w, profits, capital):
    projects = sorted(zip(capital, profits))
    heap = []
    i = 0
    n = len(projects)

    for _ in range(k):
        while i < n and projects[i][0] <= w:
            heapq.heappush(heap, -projects[i][1])
            i += 1

        if not heap:
            break

        w += -heapq.heappop(heap)

    return w
solution.timeComplexity: O(n log n + k log n)
